# The Smallest Non-Trivial $E_8$-Module

## Identifying the Representation

$E_8$ is the rank-8 exceptional Lie algebra with dimension $240 + 8 = 248$. By the complete reducibility of representations of semisimple Lie algebras, any non-trivial $E_8$-module must contain a non-trivial irreducible submodule. So I need the smallest non-trivial **irreducible** representation.

## Fundamental Representations of $E_8$

The irreducible representations are indexed by highest weights, with the fundamental ones being:

| Highest weight | Dimension |
|---|---|
| $\omega_1$ | **248** |
| $\omega_2$ | 3875 |
| $\omega_3$ | 147250 |
| $\omega_4$ | 669600 |
| $\omega_5$ | 147250 |
| $\omega_6$ | 30380 |
| $\omega_7$ | 3875 |
| $\omega_8$ | 248 |

The weight $\omega_1$ (equivalently $\omega_8$ under the outer automorphism of $E_8$) corresponds to the **highest root** of the root system. The associated irreducible representation is the **adjoint representation** $\mathfrak{e}_8$, with

$$\dim \mathfrak{e}_8 = |\Phi| + \text{rank}(E_8) = 240 + 8 = 248.$$

## Verification of Minimality

Every other non-trivial fundamental representation has dimension $\geq 30380$, and any other irreducible representation has a highest weight that is a positive integral combination of fundamental weights, so its dimension is at least as large as the smallest fundamental representation containing it. Thus **248 is indeed the minimum**.

## Conclusion

The smallest non-trivial $E_8$-module is the adjoint representation $\mathfrak{e}_8$ of dimension:

$$\boxed{248}$$
